numerical_failure.observed_behavior: np.random.zipf hangs the interpreter (does not respond to Ctrl+C) for pathological parameters: np.random.zipf(np.nan) hangs forever, and np.random.zipf(1.0000000000001) hangs for a possibly finite but very long time, because the rejection loop spends most of its time rejecting candidates X that exceed RAND_INT_MAX (X can even overflow to infinity when a is close to 1).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: np.random.zipf(np.nan) should raise an exception rather than hang; for parameters close to 1 the sampler should return values in reasonable time (the fix restricts the majorizing distribution / eliminates U values that would make X too large, giving speedups of ~1000x or more), and long computations should be interruptible by Ctrl+C (e.g. via PyErr_CheckSignals).
trigger_conditions: a very close to 1, e.g. a = 1.0000000000001, so 1/(a-1) is large and the rejection loop rejects most candidates
the legacy rejection implementation in legacy_random_zipf is used

input_output_examples.buggy_output: hangs for a possibly finite but very long time
input_output_examples.expected_output: returns sample values in reasonable time (no specific value given)

oracle_clues: Issue says the NaN case should 'probably just throw an exception'
Issue suggests calling PyErr_CheckSignals() so the computation can be cancelled
PR text notes X is rejected if it exceeds RAND_INT_MAX; zipf models a Zipf distribution truncated to RAND_INT_MAX
A later comment says the problem was fixed for NaN but remains for numbers close to 1

numerical_characteristics.precision: double (C double used for am1, b, Umin and the candidate X; the test samples are np.int64, a signed 64-bit truncation)
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: a = 1.0000000000001, i.e. within about 1e-13 of 1; n = 100000 samples in the regression test; candidate X can exceed RAND_INT_MAX and overflow to infinity when U is small
category_specific_evidence: Regression test test_zipf_a_near_1 calls zipf(1.0000000000001, size=100000) and asserts count of samples below 2**62 exceeds n/2; this checks for no hang plus a weak distribution sanity check, not a numerical tolerance
Issue gh-9829: np.random.zipf(1.0000000000001) hangs for a long time and does not respond to Ctrl+C
Rejection loop: U = 1 - next_double, X = floor(pow(U, -1/(a-1))), reject if X > RAND_INT_MAX or X < 1; the closer a is to 1, the more candidates are rejected, which causes the delay
Issue comment: a positive probability of drawing 0.0 means the loop always exits, but it may take about 1 in 2**53 draws, so the delay is extraordinarily long rather than infinite
PR #27048 fix: work backwards from RAND_INT_MAX to find the U values that make X too big and eliminate them, instead of rejecting them one by one
Legacy implementation in legacy-distributions.c restores the rejection sampler with am1 = a - 1.0, b = pow(2.0, am1), and the acceptance test V*X*(T-1)/(b-1) <= T/b
Initialisation, stopping criterion and iteration count at which behaviour differs are not stated in the passages; the loop stops only on acceptance
reproduction_risks: Without a bound the reproduction may appear to hang; a test needs a timeout or a large-sample run to observe the slowdown
